top_story.headline: Two Texas Republicans still have no 2025 annual financial disclosure on file, 60 days past the final extension
top_story.dek: Rep. Michael T. McCaul and Rep. Dan Crenshaw both filed extensions but have posted no CY2025 annual report.
paragraphs: The Deadline Watch check of every sitting member against the Clerk of the House index and Senate eFD found two members with no calendar-year 2025 annual financial disclosure on file: Rep. Michael T. McCaul (R-TX-10) and Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-2). McCaul filed an extension on 4/29/2026 and Crenshaw on 6/4/2026. The final extension date for both was 8/13/2026, so each is now 60 days past it.

The check excludes members sworn in after Nov. 1 of the report year. The tracker also notes that a filing under an unexpected spelling of a name can read as missing, so the finding rests on the index search.

Separately, the Ethics Agreement Tracker lists seven Senate-confirmed officials with no posted certification of ethics-agreement compliance more than 30 days past deadline. The longest is Michelle White Bowman, Federal Reserve Governor and Vice Chairman for Supervision, confirmed 6/4/2025 with certification due 9/2/2025, 405 days ago. No new OGE filings were identified in this window, and there are no new FARA items or financial disclosure filings.

sections.headline: No new registrations, twelve terminations, and a heavy third-quarter report day
paragraphs: 329 filings posted since 2026-10-11: 283 third-quarter reports, 32 third-quarter no-activity reports, 7 third-quarter no-activity terminations, 4 third-quarter terminations, 2 second-quarter amendments and 1 second-quarter termination. There were no new registrations. The table lists all 12 terminations plus seven activity reports with notable signals such as former officials, large spending or live fights in Washington.
Third-quarter LD-2 activity reports are due 10/20/2026, which explains the volume.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
